R4-pixellab.dc.html.title: First PixelLab art: goat, trail, sign

heading.text: Plor + Offbeat: three directions to compare

about.text:
Same 7 screens in each row: sign-in, home, question with autocomplete, safe answer, the moment you match the host, a full 7/7 run, and the share card.

Questions are the real 2026-11-02 puzzle. Host answers shown are stand-ins, not the real ones.

Colours, fonts and words like "off-key" are placeholders for the human to choose. Mix freely: e.g. B's layout with A's share card.

r2heading.text: Round 2: ten quick styles. Point at what you like

r2about.text:
Each tile: the question screen and the share card, same content every time (question 4 of 7, caught on question 5).

The ten looks were dealt at random from a library of 20 researched art directions (the design-taste-frontend skill), each with its dealt font and colours. Nothing here is a recommendation.

React any way: "I like 3's colours and 7's type", "hate all the dark ones", or a comment on a tile.

r3heading.text: Round 3: Offbeat as a climb along a cliff edge

r3about.text:
Stop 4 while typing, a safe reveal, the fall at stop 5, the friends' ridge and the share card.

The pixel art is a placeholder drawn in code, only to show where art goes. The goat, the raven host, the clouds and the colours are all open choices (D17 to D20 in the ticket).

No suggestions while typing: the word paints onto the sign instead.

Host answers are stand-ins, not the real ones. Friend names are placeholders.

r4heading.text: Round 4: real pixel art from PixelLab

r4about.text:
First tries from PixelLab (trial plan, 7 generations so far). Pick a goat, a trail and a sign, or say what to change.

Next, once you pick: the goat gets idle, hop and fall animations, and the trail gets a ledge that crumbles.

The word on the sign is page text in the pixel font, so any word fits. Sizes are a trial (64 px sprites), not a final choice (D20).

Trail A is seen from behind, not from the side, so the 7 stops would need a different layout there.

r5heading.text: Round 5: which camera? Behind the goat, or its own eyes

r5about.text:
Quick chunky sketches drawn in code (free, no PixelLab), only to compare the two cameras. Same moments for both: typing at stop 4, and getting caught at stop 5.

3rd person uses the winding-path angle you liked from Round 4: the next stops and the top flag are ahead up the ridge.

1st person puts your sign right in front, so the word is the biggest thing on screen. Friends would need a separate view here.

Pick one; then a small low-res PixelLab test (about 2 generations) for that camera.

r5lowres.text:
You picked 3rd person. The low-res PixelLab test (2 generations): the trail scene at 128 × 72 px and a goat seen from behind at 32 × 32 px, a third of Round 4’s scene width and half its goat size.

Is this chunky enough, and does it look like the game you want? If PixelLab still feels wrong, the other routes are art drawn in code (like the sketches above) or a pixel artist.

r6about.text:
Drawn in code at the sketch resolution, as you chose. Changes from your Round 5 notes:

• Clouds: three layers with rounded tops, peaks poking through, mist across the ridge, birds, and bigger cloud banks up close.
• Signs: each one is planted on a stake that stands on the stop. The host’s sign stands on its own worn stone; when you’re caught it stays on the far lip while yours falls.
• Softer colours: muted blue sky, lighter rock, dark navy instead of black, a softer red.

Colours are still placeholders (D3).
